name: bash
description: Run a shell command in the project folder. Returns stdout, stderr and exit code.

name: read_file
description: Read a text file (project folder or skill folder). Optional offset/limit in lines.

name: write_file
description: Write a text file inside the project folder (creates folders, overwrites).

name: list_dir
description: List a directory (project or skill folder).

name: ask_user
description: Ask the user 1 to 4 multiple-choice questions, shown as cards. Recommended option first. Returns the answers.

name: show_page
description: Open an HTML file in the preview pane (project or skill folder).

name: screenshot_preview
description: Take a screenshot of what the preview pane shows now and get it back as an image, to look at a contact sheet, a card page or a reel. Open the page with show_page first. Optional javascript runs in the page before the capture: to look at a reel at t seconds, set the seek slider, for example document.getElementById('seek').value = t*10; document.getElementById('seek').dispatchEvent(new Event('input')). Only describe what you actually see.

javascript.description: optional script run in the page before the capture

wait_ms.description: wait before the capture, default 600, max 5000

name: get_state
description: Read the project's state: showreel.json (decisions, gates, step, scene review), the file the user has in front of them and the top-level files. Call it before you propose anything, so you do not ask what the app already holds.

name: propose_edit
description: Offer a change to a project file (replaces its whole content). The user sees a diff and accepts or refuses; nothing is written before that, unless they switched on apply-directly for the project. Use it for prose and data files the user may be editing (brief.md, style-sheet.md, storyboard.md, showreel.json, CSV). If the answer says the file changed since, read it again and propose a new edit. Creating a new file or writing code can use write_file.

content.description: the complete new content of the file

note.description: one short line saying what changes and why, shown above the diff
